title: GrowthMate Target Architecture Implementation Prompt
prompt: You are the senior staff engineer responsible for implementing the GrowthMate target architecture in the existing repository. Read the entire repository first, including README.md, AGENTS.md, app/, tests/, frontend/, seed_data.py, buyer_agent.py, and the three binding design files: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/HIGH_LEVEL_DESIGN.md, docs/LOW_LEVEL_DESIGN.md. Treat those design files as the target specification. Do not merely describe changes: inspect the existing implementation, implement the changes, update tests, and leave the repository in a runnable state. Preserve compatible behavior and backward-compatible public endpoints where practical, but prioritize the target design over obsolete implementation details.

precedence: LOW_LEVEL_DESIGN.md for exact interfaces and behavior
HIGH_LEVEL_DESIGN.md for module boundaries and system behavior
ARCHITECTURE.md for overall principles and trade-offs
existing source code for compatibility details when not contradictory

primary_objective: Transform GrowthMate from an LLM-first shopping agent into a latency-optimized merchant growth and agent-commerce platform that increases merchant revenue while keeping every money action deterministic, explainable, bounded, gated, and auditable.
non_negotiable_principles: Do not call an LLM for deterministic work that the backend can perform exactly.
Do not call Gemini more than necessary; remove redundant post-tool LLM calls.
Do not treat external market discovery results as merchant inventory.
Only merchant-fulfillable SKUs may become payable cart items unless an explicit merchant mapping authorizes otherwise.
Cart totals, quote amounts, stock, approval, guardrails, and payment decisions must be deterministic backend logic.
Razorpay must only be reached after quote validation, explicit approval, cart integrity checks, and guardrail approval.
The LLM must never be the source of truth for payment amount or authorization.
Every material stage and money decision must be auditable without exposing chain-of-thought or secrets.

Optimize latency by avoiding unnecessary work, parallelizing independent work, caching semantically similar discovery queries, and using the least expensive intelligence path that meets the confidence requirement.
Prefer a modular monolith for the hackathon; do not introduce microservices or infrastructure complexity unless an explicit benchmark proves the need.

known_weaknesses_to_fix: Gemini is currently involved in orchestration more often than necessary.
Tool results can trigger another LLM call merely for response generation.
External search is synchronous and has a long blocking timeout.
External results can conceptually enter the mixed payable cart.
Upselling is based mainly on simple category adjacency rather than expected incremental revenue.
There is no semantic cache above SerpAPI.
There is no first-class merchant-capture scoring engine.
Conversation state is reconstructed from broad request history rather than compact durable state.
Quote/cart integrity needs to be made explicit and cryptographically tied to the payable snapshot.
Agent-commerce capability discovery and quote APIs are not yet first-class.

pipeline: merchant semantic retrieval and/or semantic external cache lookup
selective SerpAPI live discovery when justified
external candidate normalization, deduplication, filtering, and ranking
merchant-capture engine mapping buyer market intent to merchant SKUs
next-best-offer engine using expected incremental revenue and friction budget

phase_0_repository_audit: Read all current source files and tests before modifying code.
Compare current behavior with the three design files.
Identify obsolete assumptions, especially mixed external/merchant cart behavior and repeated LLM orchestration loops.
Keep a concise implementation checklist derived from the design docs.
phase_1_foundation: Refactor or create clear modules for orchestration, routing, retrieval, intelligence, growth, commerce, policy, payments, and observability.
Preserve existing endpoint compatibility where practical.
Use Decimal for final money arithmetic.
Add trace_id and stage timing support.
Add configuration values through environment variables with safe defaults.
phase_2_fast_router: Implement a local fast router that classifies intent, domain, category, complexity, risk, required action, need for merchant retrieval, need for live search, and confidence.
Use local semantic classification/embeddings where useful.
Use a lightweight structured Gemini call only when confidence is insufficient.
Never use Gemini simply to decide a simple cart operation or render deterministic search results.
phase_3_merchant_rag: Implement merchant semantic retrieval over product name, description, category, use cases, features, and compatibility metadata.
Do not encode mutable price/stock as the only semantic representation; keep price/stock as authoritative metadata.
Keep the implementation simple enough for the current catalog size, but isolate the interface so pgvector can replace it later.
phase_4_semantic_external_cache: Implement a semantic cache in front of SerpAPI.
Normalize the structured requirements and search query.
Generate a query embedding and compare against recent cached searches.
Return a cache hit only when similarity and freshness thresholds are both satisfied.
Never use external search cache as the source of truth for merchant pricing or checkout amount.
Persist successful normalized results with creation and expiry timestamps.
Handle cache corruption safely as a miss.
phase_5_async_discovery: Replace blocking SerpAPI requests with an async HTTP client such as httpx.AsyncClient.
Use a configurable timeout that is materially shorter than the current 15-second synchronous timeout.
Isolate provider parsing in an adapter.
Normalize, deduplicate, hard-filter, and rank results deterministically.
Run independent retrieval tasks concurrently where useful.
Gracefully fall back to fresh cached market results or merchant-only retrieval when SerpAPI fails.
phase_6_merchant_capture: Create Merchant Capture Engine as a first-class module.
Take buyer requirements and market candidates as input.
Apply hard constraints for stock, budget, availability, and explicit requirements.
Score candidates using configurable semantic fit, requirement fit, price fit, stock, margin, attach potential, and merchant priority factors.
Return the best merchant-fulfillable match with reason codes and an explanation.
Do not put arbitrary external products into the payable cart.
phase_7_next_best_offer: Replace hard-coded category-only upselling with a revenue-aware offer engine.
Calculate acceptance probability using historical offer events with a smoothed prior.
Calculate expected incremental revenue as accept probability × incremental margin × inventory confidence − discount cost − friction penalty.
Enforce a maximum number of offers and a maximum add-on ratio.
Return no offer when confidence or expected incremental value is too low.
phase_8_compact_state_and_orchestration: Reduce raw history passed to the LLM.
Persist compact session state where required.
Refactor LangGraph into a thin state coordinator.
Do not loop back to Gemini after every deterministic tool execution.
Use deterministic response composition for structured outcomes whenever possible.
Use one structured LLM call for complex requirement understanding rather than multiple free-form turns.
phase_9_quote_and_safe_payment: Implement a backend quote object tied to session, actor, cart version, cart hash, amount, currency, nonce, and expiry.
Create a canonical cart representation with deterministic ordering.
Require explicit approval after a checkout preview has been shown.
Validate that the current cart and current amount still match the quote.
Only after all checks pass may the Razorpay adapter be called.
Make repeated payment requests for the same valid quote safely idempotent where practical.
phase_10_agent_commerce: Ensure these APIs reuse the same commerce and policy layer as the human chat UI.
Do not allow the agent API to bypass approval or guardrails.
phase_11_observability: Add a trace_id to every request.
Measure latency for router, semantic cache, merchant retrieval, SerpAPI, Gemini, merchant capture, offer engine, DB, quote, guardrail, and Razorpay.
Record cache hit/miss, confidence, provider, result counts, errors, and stage duration.
Add a simple /metrics/latency endpoint or equivalent demo-friendly view if practical.
Never log secrets or raw payment credentials. Redact obvious PII.
phase_12_tests: Update all existing tests for changed contracts.
Add unit tests for routing and confidence thresholds.
Add semantic cache tests for exact hit, semantic hit, stale miss, low-similarity miss, and corrupt entry.
Add quote hash and cart version invalidation tests.
Add guardrail tests and explicitly assert that blocked paths never invoke Razorpay.
Add end-to-end tests for human and buyer-agent paths with external dependencies mocked.

simple_fast_path_examples: yes proceed after a current valid preview
live_search_triggers: buyer explicitly asks for market options or alternatives
merchant catalog does not have sufficient candidates
no_live_search_cases: checkout or approval operation where the merchant catalog and current cart are authoritative
fresh semantic cache hit that passes similarity and freshness thresholds

confidence_policy.medium: 0.70-0.89: one structured lightweight LLM call if needed

latency_requirements.primary_strategy: Reduce the amount of work before optimizing individual calls.
required_optimizations: avoid Gemini for deterministic cart/catalog actions
avoid SerpAPI when semantic cache is sufficiently fresh
send compact state instead of full history where possible
use structured model output with small schemas
use minimal reasoning for low-complexity model calls
cache embeddings for stable merchant products
latency_requirements.measurement: Do not claim latency improvement without measuring stage-level P50 and P95 before and after.

accuracy_requirements: Hard constraints must always be applied after semantic retrieval.
Stock and merchant price must come from the merchant database, not external search or LLM output.
A semantic cache hit must still pass freshness and confidence checks.
Low-confidence recommendation should trigger clarification or merchant-only fallback rather than a fabricated answer.
External market data must never silently override merchant price or inventory.
Offer engine may choose no offer when expected incremental value is low.

preconditions: approval is explicit and linked to the quote/current turn
transaction amount is within actor limit
session spend remains within actor limit
money_action_contract.execution: Only the payment adapter may call Razorpay, and only after all preconditions pass.
money_action_contract.blocked_behavior: Return a normal structured response with blocked=true, audit the reason, and do not call Razorpay.

rules: Expected guardrail blocks should be HTTP 200 control-flow responses unless an API contract explicitly requires otherwise.

failure_handling.gemini: On failure, fall back to deterministic routing/catalog/cart logic where possible. Never make up product, pricing, or payment facts.
failure_handling.serpapi: On timeout/error, use fresh semantic cache if available; otherwise use merchant-only retrieval with reduced-confidence messaging.
failure_handling.razorpay: Persist failed order state and tell the user no successful charge occurred unless success is confirmed by the payment flow/webhook.
failure_handling.database: Return a controlled server error for unrecoverable DB failures; do not silently claim state changed.
failure_handling.webhook: Reject invalid signatures; process valid events idempotently.

demo_requirements.normal_demo: A buyer asks for a product with a budget; GrowthMate discovers or retrieves candidates, maps the intent to a merchant SKU, suggests one high-value add-on, builds a cart, creates a quote, obtains approval, passes guardrails, and creates a Razorpay test-mode payment flow.
demo_requirements.agent_buyer_demo: An external buyer agent uses the agent-commerce endpoints instead of the human UI and still receives the same merchant discovery, quote, guardrail, and payment behavior.
demo_requirements.failure_demo: A buyer-agent transaction deliberately exceeds the configured per-transaction limit; the system returns blocked=true, explains the bound, writes the audit event, and proves that Razorpay was not called.
demo_requirements.latency_demo: Show before/after stage latency, Gemini call count, SerpAPI call count, semantic cache hit rate, and P50/P95 latency.

coding_rules: Use type hints throughout new code.
Keep guardrail and quote validation deterministic and unit-testable.
Avoid global mutable state except explicitly documented process-local caches.
Use async HTTP for external network operations in async paths.
Do not add unnecessary dependencies; reuse installed packages when possible.
Do not duplicate pricing logic across layers.
Use one canonical source of truth for cart total.
Do not persist raw secrets or sensitive request contents in audit logs.
definition_of_done: All design-required modules are implemented or intentionally mapped to existing compatible modules.
New tests cover routing, semantic cache, merchant capture, offer scoring, quote integrity, policy, and dependency failures.
Simple operations avoid unnecessary Gemini calls.
SerpAPI is skipped on valid semantic cache hits.
External products cannot be charged directly unless explicitly mapped to merchant inventory.
Merchant Capture Engine produces explainable mapping decisions.
Next Best Offer Engine optimizes expected incremental revenue with a friction budget.
Every payment attempt is quote-bound, approval-bound, guardrail-bound, and auditable.
At least one end-to-end blocked payment test proves the Razorpay adapter is not invoked.
Latency and cache metrics are visible enough to compare before/after.
README and design docs are updated to match the actual implementation.
The app can be started locally with the documented commands and no hidden manual steps.
final_response_required_from_opencode: After implementation, report: files changed, architecture changes, latency optimizations, new APIs, test results, any design deviations, and exact commands to run the demo and tests. Do not claim a feature is complete unless it is implemented and tested.
